pr.title: fix(decode): reject unsupported CUDA-core split disabling
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Reject `disable_split_kv=True` when `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` resolves to CUDA-core decode. That planner has no disable-split argument, so `plan()`, `workspace_size()`, and `fast_decode_plan()` previously accepted the option while silently leaving split scheduling enabled.

The error is raised before metadata transfer or compiled planning. The default `False` and supported FA2 tensor-core controls remain unchanged; the message directs callers that need the option to `use_tensor_cores=True, backend="fa2"`. Auto cuDNN resolution remains ahead of this check. A rejected CUDA-core replan preserves the previous valid cuDNN route, so the wrapper can still run its existing plan.

`workspace_size()` also rejects the cuTile backend with `NotImplementedError`, consistently with the existing unsupported-backend gate. cuTile planning bypasses the C++ planner and its run path allocates scratch internally; querying the CUDA-core module would report another backend's buffer requirements. This applies with the split flag both off and on, and leaves ordinary cuTile `plan()` behavior unchanged.

**Release note (compatibility):** CUDA-core decode now raises `ValueError` for `disable_split_kv=True` in `plan()`, `fast_decode_plan()`, and `workspace_size()`; these calls previously ignored the flag. Use `backend="fa2", use_tensor_cores=True` to disable splitting, or retain `disable_split_kv=False` for CUDA-core decode. The same migration note is included in the rendered attention API documentation.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Related to the `disable_split_kv` side note in #5107. This does not close the issue's FP32-partial precision problem or replace #5166, which changes the split partial buffers rather than the Python flag contract.

Current rebase on main `9df33e23`, final head `a08d5ee6`:

- Reproduced the reported planner-argument assertion on rebased `cf8b036e`: **12 failed, 32 passed**. Indexing `disable_split_kv` from the front (15 for workspace sizing, 17 for both planning entry points) gives **44 passed, 0 skipped** with the same suite. The Boolean identity assertion still checks both flag values, all three entry points, and both metadata modes.
- RTX 5060 Ti / SM120, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA toolkit 13.2: fresh source JIT in an isolated cache passed **6 expected CUDA-core rejections and 12 FP64 forward comparisons**. B1/Hq8/Hkv2/D128/page16/S256, FP16/NHD; CUDA-core default and FA2 tensor-core with flag off/on, each in both metadata modes. Maximum absolute error: 0.0001448553; maximum NRMSE: 0.0003287165. This uses the same probe and numerical thresholds as the earlier validation.


<summary>Historical validation before this rebase (published head 9e13a030)</summary>

Added actual-public-API CPU regression tests for all three entry points, default/tensor-core controls, validation before metadata copies, and cuDNN/cuTile/auto dispatch boundaries. Validation:
- Normal upstream pytest collection: 44 CPU public-API tests passed (2 existing Cutlass deprecation warnings). The prior 36-case suite failed in 4 rejected-replan cases against the initial PR implementation and passed after route preservation. The final 44-case suite fails in all 8 new cuTile workspace-query cases against `8bc2096`, then all 44 pass after adding cuTile to the unsupported-query gate. The new cases cover both split-flag values, tensor-core flags, and wrapper metadata modes, and reject before metadata transfer or module selection. The rejected-replan cases create a valid cuDNN auto plan, reject a CUDA-core replan through `plan()` or `fast_decode_plan()`, and verify that the existing plan still routes to cuDNN through a backend spy. They do not execute cuDNN kernels.
- RTX 5060 Ti, SM120, Torch 2.13.0+cu130; JIT kernels built from the pinned source checkout and reused for the Python-only review fix: all 6 fresh-wrapper unsupported calls raised the expected `ValueError`. This smoke was rerun on the final Python implementation.

- Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed. The full repository hooks and full hardware test matrix were not run.

No graph capture/replay or performance claim. The GPU smoke validates a small supported case, not every device/shape.

## Reviewer Notes

The cuTile follow-up is documented: `plan()` currently ignores this flag on that backend. Its execution behavior is unchanged in this patch. The public parameter docs now distinguish FA2 tensor-core and CuTe-DSL planning support from CUDA-core rejection.

This deliberately changes an unsupported combination from silent acceptance to `ValueError`; it does not add no-split support to the CUDA-core scheduler. A custom caller that passes `disable_split_kv=True` on CUDA-core decode will now fail. The source audit below narrows the known downstream exposure; it does **not** make the API behavior change globally non-breaking or settle release/deprecation policy.

<details>
<summary>Downstream compatibility: pinned source audit, 2026-10-14</summary>

| Project / inspected revision | Actual flag and wrapper path | Exposure to the new CUDA-core rejection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vLLM `8a8e2baa` | Batch invariance can set [`disable_split_kv=True`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8a8e2baa02cdd3d98ee99dbead0a8c9943a97410/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py#L760-L767). Both eager and CUDA-graph `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` constructors explicitly set [`use_tensor_cores=True`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8a8e2baa02cdd3d98ee99dbead0a8c9943a97410/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py#L1311-L1348); regular and fast planning preserve that wrapper. | No affected call identified in this revision. |
| SGLang `c82e8bd5` | Ordinary decode passes `False`. Graph decode passes `True` only in the [deterministic branch, which first forces tensor cores](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c82e8bd5fe9cad787c2cd3ccf067a1ba5b95e0c4/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py#L411-L425). Both [eager](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c82e8bd5fe9cad787c2cd3ccf067a1ba5b95e0c4/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py#L523-L530) and [graph wrappers](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c82e8bd5fe9cad787c2cd3ccf067a1ba5b95e0c4/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py#L1102-L1114) use that selection with FA2. Multi-step draft and fast-plan replay preserve the same relation. | No affected call identified in this revision. |
| TensorRT-LLM `78313690` | The ordinary batch decode [`plan()` passes literal `False`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/783136904ce2b03303fca05dc74412989ea67fb2/tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/flashinfer.py#L2242-L2304), even when CUDA cores are selected. CSA2's `True` calls use FA2 [ragged prefill](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/783136904ce2b03303fca05dc74412989ea67fb2/tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/sparse/csa2/backend.py#L745-L792) and [paged prefill](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/783136904ce2b03303fca05dc74412989ea67fb2/tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/sparse/csa2/backend.py#L808-L851) wrappers. | These calls do not reach the new rejection. CSA2's `True` sites are separate prefill APIs. |

This is static control/data-flow inspection at the linked commits, not an end-to-end run of these three engines with this patch. It does not cover all historical releases, forks, custom integrations, or unrelated backend compatibility. No affected built-in call was identified in the inspected paths, so this revision retains the explicit error; callers outside this audit remain subject to the behavior change above.

</details>

Prepared with AI assistance; the API change, backend boundaries, cuTile scratch ownership, and scope of the tests have been reviewed.

+"""CPU-only validation of decode split flags at the planner boundary."""
+
+from contextlib import nullcontext
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import flashinfer.decode as decode
+
+
+def _wrapper(monkeypatch, use_tensor_cores, use_cuda_graph, backend="fa2"):
+    # Pinned allocation needs a CUDA driver even with CPU tensors. Keep the
+    # real constructor and public methods, but use unpinned CPU buffers here.
+    empty = torch.empty
+
+    def cpu_empty(*args, **kwargs):
+        kwargs.pop("pin_memory", None)
+        return empty(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch, "empty", cpu_empty)
+    wrapper = decode.BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(
+        torch.empty(1024, dtype=torch.uint8),
+        use_tensor_cores=use_tensor_cores,
+        use_cuda_graph=use_cuda_graph,
+        paged_kv_indptr_buffer=torch.empty(2, dtype=torch.int32),
+        paged_kv_indices_buffer=torch.empty(4, dtype=torch.int32),
+        paged_kv_last_page_len_buffer=torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.int32),
+        backend=backend,
+    )
+    calls = []
+
+    def plan(*args):
+        calls.append(("plan", args))
+        return []
+
+    def workspace_size(*args):
+        calls.append(("workspace_size", args))
+        return 0, 0
+
+    module = SimpleNamespace(plan=plan, workspace_size=workspace_size)
+    wrapper._jit_module = module
+    wrapper._cached_module = module
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "device", lambda device: nullcontext())
+    return wrapper, calls
+
+
+def _call(wrapper, entrypoint, disable_split_kv, **extra):
+    args = (
+        torch.tensor([0, 4], dtype=torch.int32),
+        torch.arange(4, dtype=torch.int32),
+        torch.tensor([16], dtype=torch.int32),
+        8,
+        2,
+        128,
+        16,
+    )
+    kwargs = {"q_data_type": torch.float16, "disable_split_kv": disable_split_kv}
+    kwargs.update(extra)
+    if entrypoint == "fast_decode_plan":
+        return decode.fast_decode_plan(wrapper, *args, **kwargs)
+    return getattr(wrapper, entrypoint)(*args, **kwargs)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("entrypoint", ["plan", "workspace_size", "fast_decode_plan"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+def test_cuda_core_decode_rejects_disable_split_kv(
+    monkeypatch, entrypoint, use_cuda_graph
+):
+    wrapper, calls = _wrapper(monkeypatch, False, use_cuda_graph)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="disable_split_kv.*CUDA-core decode"):
+        _call(wrapper, entrypoint, True)
+    assert not calls, "unsupported option must not reach the compiled planner"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("entrypoint", ["plan", "workspace_size", "fast_decode_plan"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+def test_cuda_core_decode_default_still_reaches_planner(
+    monkeypatch, entrypoint, use_cuda_graph
+):
+    wrapper, calls = _wrapper(monkeypatch, False, use_cuda_graph)
+    _call(wrapper, entrypoint, False)
+    assert len(calls) == 1
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("entrypoint", ["plan", "workspace_size", "fast_decode_plan"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("disable_split_kv", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+def test_tensor_core_decode_preserves_disable_split_kv(
+    monkeypatch, entrypoint, disable_split_kv, use_cuda_graph
+):
+    wrapper, calls = _wrapper(monkeypatch, True, use_cuda_graph)
+    _call(wrapper, entrypoint, disable_split_kv)
+    assert len(calls) == 1
+    # workspace_size omits the two integer workspace buffers used by planning.
+    # Index from the front so appending FA2 options does not shift the flag.
+    disable_split_kv_index = 15 if entrypoint == "workspace_size" else 17
+    assert calls[0][1][disable_split_kv_index] is disable_split_kv
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+def test_rejected_plan_does_not_copy_metadata(monkeypatch, use_cuda_graph):
+    wrapper, calls = _wrapper(monkeypatch, False, use_cuda_graph)
+
+    def unexpected_copy(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("invalid split flag reached metadata transfer")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.Tensor, "to", unexpected_copy)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.Tensor, "copy_", unexpected_copy)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="disable_split_kv.*CUDA-core decode"):
+        _call(wrapper, "plan", True)
+    assert not calls
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["cudnn", "cutile"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+def test_other_backends_are_not_classified_as_cuda_core(
+    monkeypatch, backend, use_cuda_graph
+):
+    wrapper, calls = _wrapper(monkeypatch, False, use_cuda_graph, backend)
+    cudnn_calls = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(wrapper, "_plan_cudnn", lambda *args: cudnn_calls.append(args))
+    _call(wrapper, "plan", True)
+    assert not wrapper.use_tensor_cores
+    assert not calls
+    assert len(cudnn_calls) == (1 if backend == "cudnn" else 0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("entrypoint", ["plan", "fast_decode_plan"])
+def test_auto_cudnn_resolution_precedes_cuda_core_validation(monkeypatch, entrypoint):
+    wrapper, calls = _wrapper(monkeypatch, False, False, "auto")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(wrapper, "_auto_prefers_cudnn", lambda *args, **kwargs: True)
+    cudnn_calls = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(wrapper, "_plan_cudnn", lambda *args: cudnn_calls.append(args))
+    _call(wrapper, entrypoint, True, q_len_per_req=2)
+    assert wrapper._cudnn_auto
+    assert len(cudnn_calls) == 1
+    assert not calls
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_tensor_cores", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("disable_split_kv", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+def test_cutile_workspace_query_does_not_use_another_backend(
+    monkeypatch, use_tensor_cores, disable_split_kv, use_cuda_graph
+):
+    wrapper, calls = _wrapper(monkeypatch, use_tensor_cores, use_cuda_graph, "cutile")
+    wrapper._jit_module = None
+
+    def unexpected_backend(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("cuTile workspace query reached another backend's module")
+
+    def unexpected_copy(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("unsupported workspace query reached metadata transfer")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(decode, "get_batch_decode_module", unexpected_backend)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(decode, "get_batch_prefill_module", unexpected_backend)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.Tensor, "to", unexpected_copy)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.Tensor, "copy_", unexpected_copy)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="workspace_size.*cutile"):
+        _call(wrapper, "workspace_size", disable_split_kv)
+    assert not calls
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("entrypoint", ["plan", "fast_decode_plan"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+def test_rejected_replan_preserves_active_cudnn_route(
+    monkeypatch, entrypoint, use_cuda_graph
+):
+    """Reject a CUDA-core replan without invalidating the working cuDNN plan."""
+    wrapper, calls = _wrapper(monkeypatch, False, use_cuda_graph, "auto")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(wrapper, "_auto_prefers_cudnn", lambda *args, **kwargs: True)
+    cudnn_calls = []
+
+    def plan_cudnn(*args):
+        wrapper._cudnn_kv_lens_view = torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32).view(
+            1, 1, 1, 1
+        )
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(wrapper, "_plan_cudnn", plan_cudnn)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(decode, "_CUDNN_GRAPH_AVAILABLE", False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        decode,
+        "cudnn_batch_decode_with_kv_cache",
+        lambda *args, **kwargs: cudnn_calls.append(kwargs),
+    )

# CI workflow using AWS self-hosted runners.
# Runs AOT build tests, GPU unit tests and the CPU-only tests/cpu suite on PRs
# to main, and on main itself on a schedule.
# Uses ci/bash.sh for Docker execution (same as Jenkins).
#
# Permission Control:
# - main: a scheduled full-suite run three times a day (not per merge). Per-merge
#   runs shared one cancel-in-progress group, so each merge cancelled the last:
#   about 90% of them never finished. A scheduled run is never cancelled, runs
#   every lane to completion (no fail-fast), and a failure opens or updates a
#   tracking issue; the next green run closes it.
# - PRs: run when 'run-ci' or the bot's 'run-ci-focused' label is applied.
#   Applying the label is the trigger, so new commits need a new trigger:
#   @flashinfer-bot run.
#
# Instance Purchasing:
# - All runners are on-demand. Spot was removed.
# - A failure here is a real failure, so there is nothing to retry
#   automatically.
# - On-demand capacity is billed for as long as it runs, so the first failure
#   should stop everything else. GitHub only fail-fasts within one matrix, so
#   all tests live in a single matrix built by the setup job. They still start
#   in parallel; the matrix exists purely to make the cancellation global.

name: PR Test

on:
  # Off the 00:00 UTC nightly-release slot; one run per Asia / EU / US workday.
  # Minute 17, not 0: GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs at the top of the hour.
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 4,12,20 * * *'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      skip_aot:
        description: 'Skip AOT build tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip_gpu:
        description: 'Skip GPU tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # A label other than run-ci can never start tests, so it gets its own group and
  # does not cancel - otherwise label churn would discard running GPU jobs.
  # Scheduled runs on main get their own group and never cancel each other: at
  # most one runs and one waits, so a slow run delays the next instead of wasting
  # itself.
  group: pr-test-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled-' || '' }}${{ github.ref }}${{ (github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') && '-noop' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && !(github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: read # reads the ci/test-scope status published by ci-bot-commands.yml
  actions: read

env:
  EXECUTOR_NUMBER: "0"
  SKIP_CI_PATTERNS: '\.md$|^docs/|^docker/|^licenses/|^LICENSE$|^NOTICE$|^benchmarks/|^\.github/CODEOWNERS$'

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gate - Check if PR is authorized to run CI
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  gate:
    name: Permission Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      authorized: ${{ steps.check.outputs.authorized }}
    steps:
      - name: Check authorization
        id: check
        env:
          # Read via env, not inlined: a label name is caller-supplied text.
          EVENT_ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
        run: |
          # Always allow scheduled runs on main and workflow_dispatch
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Not a PR, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Authorize on run-ci being applied, not on it being present: presence
          # would re-authorize every later push, which is the auto-trigger this
          # gate removes.
          if [[ "$EVENT_ACTION" == "labeled" && ( "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci" || "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci-focused" ) ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "$LABEL_NAME label applied, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Not triggered by the run-ci label, skipping CI"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Setup - Read docker tag and check if build should be skipped
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    name: Setup
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docker_tag: ${{ steps.get-tag.outputs.tag }}
      skip_build: ${{ steps.check.outputs.skip }}
      test_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
      test_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.count }}
      # Surfaced so the required check can say a green result was scoped.
      test_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
      h100_disabled: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.h100_disabled }}
      spec_lint_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_matrix }}
      spec_lint_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_count }}
      checkout_sha: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.checkout_sha || github.sha }}
      snapshot_base: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_base }}
      snapshot_tree: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Built here rather than written inline in the test job because the
      # `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` publishes the requested scope as a `ci/test-scope`
      # commit status on this SHA (see ci-bot-commands.yml). Read it verbatim - the
      # comment was parsed once, there, and nothing is re-parsed here.
      #
      # Statuses come back newest-first, so the newest for this context is the last
      # command issued. No status means nobody asked for a scope: run the full suite.
      # Because the status is keyed to the SHA, a scope cannot outlive the commit it was
      # requested for.
      - name: Read requested test scope
        id: scope
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          EVENT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'run-ci-focused' }}
        run: |
          # The combined endpoint (/status, not /statuses) returns one entry per
          # context, already the latest. Using it means re-triggering overwrites
          # cleanly without this step deduplicating by hand, and without depending on
          # the raw list's ordering, which is not a documented guarantee.
          STATUSES=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/status")
          SCOPE=$(jq -r '
              .statuses
              | map(select(.context | test("^ci/test-scope-[0-9]+$")))
              | map({n: (.context | sub("^ci/test-scope-"; "") | tonumber),
                     d: (.description // "")})
              | sort_by(.n) | map(.d) | map(select(. != "")) | join(" ")' <<< "$STATUSES")
          SNAPSHOT=$(jq -r '[.statuses[] | select(.context == "ci/test-snapshot")][0].description // ""' <<< "$STATUSES")
          if [ "${REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT:-false}" = true ] && [ -z "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            echo "::error::Automatic test snapshot was cleared or is missing. Issue a new bot run command."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            if [[ ! "$SNAPSHOT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{16}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Invalid automatic test snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            read -r SELECTED_BASE SELECTED_MERGE SELECTED_TREE SELECTED_SCOPE <<< "$SNAPSHOT"
            ACTUAL_SCOPE=$(printf '%s' "$SCOPE" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
            if [ "$ACTUAL_SCOPE" != "$SELECTED_SCOPE" ]; then
              echo "::error::The automatic scope does not match its snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            # Reconstruct the selected source independently of GitHub's merge ref.
            # No PR scripts, hooks, or submodule contents run during preparation.
            for sha in "$SELECTED_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA"; do
              git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$sha"
            done
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$HEAD_SHA"
            ACTUAL_TREE=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
            if [ "$ACTUAL_TREE" != "$SELECTED_TREE" ]; then
              echo "::error::Merged source differs from AI-selected tree. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Verified AI-selected tree $ACTUAL_TREE (selection $SELECTED_MERGE)"
            echo "checkout_sha=${HEAD_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_base=${SELECTED_BASE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_tree=${SELECTED_TREE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "checkout_sha=${EVENT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ -z "$SCOPE" ]; then
            echo "No requested scope for ${HEAD_SHA}; running the full suite"
          else
            echo "Requested scope: ${SCOPE}"
          fi
          echo "test_path=${SCOPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Validate CUDA configuration
        run: python3 ci/validate_cuda_versions.py

      # A shard script that no longer parses fails here, on the PR that changed it,
      # instead of silently un-scheduling later targeted A10G/T4 runs.
      - name: Validate bare-run coverage parse
        run: |
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part{1,2,3,4,5}.sh
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh

      - name: Get Docker Tag
        id: get-tag
        run: |
          TAG=$(grep 'flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu129:' ci/docker-tags.yml | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')
          if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to extract Docker tag from ci/docker-tags.yml"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Docker tag: $TAG"

      - name: Load runtime CUDA matrix
        id: cuda-versions
        run: echo "runtime=$(jq -c '.runtime' ci/cuda-versions.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Check Skip Conditions
        id: check
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            echo "skip=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Build Test Matrix

          SKIP_GPU: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_gpu }}
          RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX: ${{ steps.cuda-versions.outputs.runtime }}
